inputs.source: Nightly batch of CRM account rows (40,000 rows/night; ~3 percent have malformed company names that never resolve)

instructions.note: "Keep going until every row is complete" sets no limit on steps, retries, runtime, or number of spawned sub-agents. Combined with the runtime note that ~3 percent of the 40,000 nightly rows have malformed company names that never return a complete result, this instruction guarantees a non-terminating retry/spawn loop every night against a billed, shared-quota API.
"If a lookup fails or looks incomplete" gives the model no objective completion criterion, so the decision to retry or spawn a researcher is left entirely to model judgment with no backstop.

controls.name: Bounded retry count per row
controls.decay_rationale: A hard retry ceiling enforced by the orchestrator, not the model, does not weaken as model capability changes.

controls.name: Sub-agent spawn depth and fan-out limit
controls.decay_rationale: An orchestrator-enforced cap on spawn depth and count blocks recursive spawning regardless of what the model decides.

controls.name: Max unattended steps and runtime limit for the batch job
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced outside the model at the orchestration layer.

controls.name: Per-run and per-day spend/call cap on enrich.lookup
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the API gateway or billing layer, not by model compliance.

controls.name: Dedicated API key/quota for the enrichment agent, isolated from sales and marketing
controls.decay_rationale: Isolating the credential and quota bounds the blast radius structurally; it does not depend on the model behaving.

controls.name: Real-time spend/quota consumption alert
controls.decay_rationale: A monitoring threshold independent of the model's own reporting.

controls.name: Quarantine a row after N failed attempts instead of retrying or spawning indefinitely
controls.decay_rationale: A hard attempt counter enforced outside the model's own judgment of 'looks incomplete'.

findings.title: Unbounded spend loop against a shared enrichment quota (TC6 spend loop)

attack_path.note: Nightly batch of 40,000 CRM rows; ~3 percent have malformed company names that never return a complete lookup result.

Prompt instructs the agent to retry on failure and 'keep going until every row is complete', with no retry cap, spend cap, or step limit, against an API billed per call that shares its monthly quota with sales and marketing.

forecast.watch_signal: Monthly consumption rate against the shared enrich.lookup quota; watch for nightly batch runtime or row counts growing, or additional teams/agents being added to the same shared key.

evidence.observation: "There is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents."

"enrich.lookup is billed per call. The API key and its monthly quota are shared with the sales and marketing teams; when the quota runs out, their tools stop working until the next month." and "There is no spend alert on the enrichment account."
"Roughly 3 percent of rows have malformed company names that never return a complete result", which guarantees repeated retries every night under the current prompt instructions.
"If a lookup fails or looks incomplete, retry, or spawn a researcher sub agent... Keep going until every row is complete."

recommendations.action: Add a hard per-run and per-day spend/call cap on cap.enrich_lookup that halts the batch automatically when exceeded.
Issue the enrichment agent a dedicated API key and quota isolated from the sales and marketing teams so a runaway loop cannot disable their tools.
After a fixed number of failed attempts per row (for example 3), mark the row for manual review and stop retrying, instead of continuing indefinitely.
Add real-time spend/quota consumption alerting at a threshold well below the shared monthly cap.

findings.title: Unbounded recursive sub-agent spawning with no depth or count limit

attack_path.note: Same nightly batch of 40,000 rows feeds row-by-row processing.
Lookup fails or 'looks incomplete' for malformed or otherwise ambiguous rows.
Agent spawns a researcher sub-agent per failing row; sub-agents can themselves spawn further researchers recursively, with no depth or total-count limit declared anywhere in the design.

forecast.watch_signal: Count and depth of concurrently active sub-agents spawned per nightly run; watch for any increase in the set of tools available to spawned researchers.

evidence.observation: "There is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents. Sub agents can spawn their own researchers."
"...spawn a researcher sub agent to investigate the account" is offered as an unconditional alternative to retrying, with no guidance limiting how many times this can happen.

recommendations.action: Impose a hard maximum spawn depth (for example, no researcher may itself spawn a researcher) and a total spawn count cap per nightly batch.
Set max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes for the batch job and for every spawned sub-agent.
Monitor active sub-agent count in real time and auto-terminate the batch run if it exceeds a budgeted threshold.

rating.rationale: Both the enrichment lookup (a billed, shared-quota spend action) and sub-agent spawning (recursive delegation) are S3-severe sinks reached directly from an internal but unbounded input: 40,000 rows/night with a deterministic ~3 percent failure rate that the prompt instructs the agent to retry or escalate against 'until every row is complete', with no step, retry, spend, or spawn-depth limit anywhere in the design. Per the rubric's autonomy modifier (A4_fully_autonomous, can_spawn_agents true, no step/runtime cap), both findings' base tier of high is raised one tier to critical. No declared or verified controls exist on either path (only missing_recommended ones), so residual equals inherent at critical for both findings, and the rollup rating is critical/critical/critical. Because no controls currently exist, no forecast trigger can further defeat anything; forecast stays at critical and mainly flags that growth in batch size, runtime, or spawn permissions would not be caught by anything in the current design. The single most consequential gap is the absence of any spend cap or dedicated/isolated quota on cap.enrich_lookup (ctl.spend_cap / ctl.dedicated_quota): without it, a design flaw with no adversary involved can exhaust a quota shared with sales and marketing, taking down their tooling for the rest of the month.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design in prompt.md and the provided runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior; actual nightly runs were not instrumented or reviewed.

No tool manifest or MCP/API configuration was provided for enrich.lookup or the sub-agent spawning mechanism; capability scope and credential_scope for cap.spawn_researcher and cap.crm_write are inferred from prose and recorded with lower confidence than cap.enrich_lookup.
No historical cost or quota burn-rate data was provided; the severity of the quota-exhaustion consequence is based on the stated shared-quota design rather than measured spend history.
